parts.text:
8
The graph shows how a physical quantity varies with time.
quantity
time
0
0
Which event could best be represented by the graph?
A
the acceleration of a firework rising to a maximum height and falling to the ground
B
the acceleration of a skydiver leaving an aircraft, falling, opening a parachute and falling to
the ground
C
the speed of a javelin as it leaves an athlete’s hand, falls and sinks into the ground
D
the speed of a high jump athlete leaving the ground, jumping over a bar and descending to
the ground

hints: Look at the sign of the quantity: it starts positive, reaches zero, stays at zero, then suddenly becomes negative before returning to zero.
Recall that speed cannot be negative while acceleration can be positive for downwards and negative for upwards, so check which options are ruled out by the part below the time axis.
Think how net force and $a = (mg - drag)/m$ change for a falling skydiver first with small drag then with a large parachute drag.
walkthrough: First read the shape: the quantity starts at a maximum positive value, curves down to zero, stays at zero for a time, then jumps suddenly to a negative value and curves back up to zero.
Speed is defined as distance per unit time with no direction, so $speed \ge 0$. Any graph that goes below the time axis cannot be speed, which removes the javelin and high-jump options.
That leaves acceleration, where positive can mean downwards and negative can mean upwards. Acceleration follows $a = F_{net}/m$.

For the first fall, weight $mg$ acts down and drag acts up and grows with speed. So $a = g - drag/m$ starts near $g$ and decreases to $0$ when drag equals weight at terminal velocity, matching the first decay to zero.

When the parachute opens, drag suddenly becomes much larger than weight, so net force and acceleration are suddenly upwards - negative. As speed falls, drag falls until a slower terminal velocity is reached and $a$ returns to $0$, matching the sharp negative spike decaying to zero.
Only the skydiver leaving the aircraft, reaching terminal velocity, then opening a parachute to reach a second terminal velocity shows this sequence. This is option B

A.explanation: A firework in free flight has acceleration about $-g$ throughout, not a positive value decaying to zero then a sharp negative spike.

B.explanation: Initial fall gives large downward acceleration that falls to zero at terminal velocity, then opening the parachute gives a large upward - negative - acceleration that returns to zero at a new terminal velocity.

C.explanation: Speed is a scalar that cannot be negative, so it cannot go below the time axis as this graph does after the parachute-like drop.

D.explanation: Speed is always zero or positive and for a high jump it would fall to zero at the top then increase, not start at a maximum and show a negative section.
